slides.texte_overlay:
How to speak so clearly
people hang on every word
Know your point before you speak. Ask yourself "what do I want them to remember?" and say that first. Clear thinking always comes before clear speaking.
Open your mouth a bit more. Mumbling comes from lazy lips and jaw. Pronouncing each word fully makes you sound confident and easy to follow.
Use examples instead of explanations. "It's like when you..." A concrete picture makes people understand you in seconds. Practise it with a friend.
Lower your voice at the end of a sentence. Rising tones sound unsure. Ending low sounds certain and makes people take you seriously.
Read and learn a little every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it gives me better words and clearer ideas.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It gives me better words and clearer ideas.

slides.texte_overlay: Record yourself once a week. Listen back for rushed parts and filler words. Hearing yourself is the fastest way to improve how you speak.
Look at people while you talk. Eye contact keeps them with you, and it helps you notice when someone has lost the thread. Then you adapt.
